deities: Lord Ganesha (7.5 ft tall, 4 ft wide idol adorned with nearly 8 kg of gold); Jay and Vijay, the marble sentinels, guard the entrance
festivals: Ganesh Chaturthi (Ganeshotsav) - the temple is the birthplace of the public Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav tradition

history.dynasty: None (built by private merchant Dagadusheth Halwai; completed 1893)
history.summary: One of India's most famous Ganesha temples, built by the sweet-maker (halwai) Dagadusheth Gadve, a Lingayat trader from Karnataka who settled in Pune and grew rich selling sweets (his original shop survives as Kaka Halwai near Datta Mandir). In the late 1800s Dagadusheth lost his only son in a plague epidemic, and he and his wife Lakshmibai sank into depression; their guru Shri Madhavnath Maharaj advised them to build a Ganesha temple to heal themselves, and it was completed in 1893. Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, a close friend of Dagadusheth, visited the temple and was struck by its construction and his friend's dedication; the idea of celebrating Ganesh Chaturthi as a public festival - Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav - as a platform for the freedom movement was born here, an epoch-making event in Indian history. The temple is maintained by the Shrimant Dagadusheth Ganpati Trust. (Some sources give the founder's origin as Nashik; 'Nashik' and 'Karnataka' versions of his origin both appear in web sources.)

name: Dagadusheth Halwai Ganapati Temple
town_description: Pune is the cultural capital of Maharashtra, in Budhwar Peth in the old city at the temple. Known for Marathi culture, education ('Oxford of the East'), and the grand 11-day Ganeshotsav from Ganesh Chaturthi to Anant Chaturdashi in the Hindu month of Bhadrapada.

travel.road: In Budhwar Peth in the city centre; easily reached by auto, taxi, or city bus. Car parking is a problem - park elsewhere and walk (per visitor reviews).

visitor_information.best_time: August-September for Ganesh Chaturthi; October to March for comfortable weather.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open daily (exact hours not confirmed from sources - verify locally). Daily pooja, abhisheka, and aarti are held. The temple is constructed so openly that the idol can be seen even from outside.
